review

body: bash checks/run fails two checks outside this stage: ceremony-surfaces (checks/run still runs checks/ceremony-surfaces, which s-backout removed; WI 8) and materialized-standalone on plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:1297, a prose comment (s-tasks is running). Every other check passes, and materialized-standalone reports nothing for plumbline or ports.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/issues:398 and :1207 carry comments the lint rejects (comment-hygiene), so bash checks/run fails materialized-standalone; the file is modified in the working tree outside s-corpus's files.

The run's brief says new annotations may go in the family's scripts, but checks/materialized-standalone refuses any @decision:/@story: comment in a payload script (scripts/issues among them), since the consumer's lint has no such citation declared. This stage adds none to scripts/issues; later stages that touch payload scripts meet the same check.

owner-list.md 'Close the issues the run resolved' closes an issue only for a defect at verified or a report rejected gone or left alone. A backlog defect a fixer declined and a verifier accepted (now declined with verified) closes nothing and is filed nowhere, so its issue stays open and the next run takes it up and declines it again; A9, the intake keeps reporting a defect the run judged not real. Stood the same before this stage (declines were never verified).

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md step 4d and the issue definition it transcludes. Step 4d reads 'Findings still open at the cap → issues.' (also 5d, and line 40 'Findings still open at the cap become issues (kind discover)'). Phase 1 reviewer findings are scaffolding fixes under _discover/ (template conformance, depth, file:line citations, coverage), not questions about the corpus; step 9 then archives _discover/ to history/discover/, so the filed issue outlives the material it names, and no option can be a durable corpus mutation as the issue format requires. The transcluded {{ISSUE-DEFINITION}} (skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md) says 'Judgment items and defects outside a run's scope become issues. Fix mechanical findings in-cycle and file none.' The story promises 'a queue of judgment questions, so that my design attention is spent resolving genuine ambiguities'; a session following step 4d puts unfixed mechanical scaffolding findings into the owner's queue as judgment questions. Scripts it calls ran clean on a scratch project (issues list/file/show, catalog-toc, the archive moves).

Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md step 6c: 'Further thin-discovery needs become issues; the back-edge never loops.' The Phase 2 Reviewer prompt in the same file defines a thin discovery request as one whose fix 'is "read more code". A fix that is "make a design decision" is an issue.' and says 'Do not use the block for findings already addressed, for owner-judgment issues'. Step 6c turns those read-more-code needs into intake issues anyway, which the issue definition ('Judgment items and defects outside a run's scope become issues') does not admit. The story promises 'a queue of judgment questions, so that my design attention is spent resolving genuine ambiguities'; a session following step 6c files requests to read more code as questions for the owner.

body: Reviewed /plan-sprint (SKILL.md Draft, core.md code planner step 8), the sprint build prompt's documentation rule (_sprint/shared.md), and certification's documentation pass (converge/prompts/sprint-review.md, sprint-pass.md) for an owner declaring a new kind of documentation through a '### New docspec: <slug>' delta. The documentation match reads only the live index: SKILL.md:105 'Where .ok-planner/docspec/ exists, read the docspec index at .ok-planner/docspec.md ... a docspec whose references include a corpus artifact a work item or delta names, or a code path the owner names for the work, is touched. Add one work item per touched docspec'. A docspec drafted as a delta in this same sprint is not in the index (catalog-toc regenerates it only when the delta is applied at execution), and nothing says a New docspec delta itself makes its docspec touched; code planning (core.md step 8) matches only 'a path under Changes falls under one of its code-path references' against the same index. The builder writes documentation only where 'A builder whose work item names docspec:<slug>' (_sprint/shared.md DOCUMENTATION-RULE), and certification files a documentation pass only 'per docspec a work item names' (sprint-review.md:26). So the sprint that declares the new docspec applies the file and writes none of the documentation it orders, and no later run writes it until some unrelated change happens to reach one of its references. The story promises: 'a way to declare each kind of documentation my project keeps ... so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; decision sprints-write-the-documentation: 'adds one work item for each docspec the work touches'. Saw: a newly declared kind of documentation has no writer in the declaring sprint, and certification never checks it against the order. Scripts side checked: in a scratch project, catalog-toc listed a new docspec ('- `ddoc-readme` — where: README.md; references: story:ddoc-export, `src/cli.py`') only after the file was written.

Reviewed /plan-sprint for an owner who changes whom an existing kind of documentation is for (or what it covers) through an '### Amend docspec: <slug>' delta. The documentation match (SKILL.md:105) touches a docspec only where 'its references include a corpus artifact a work item or delta names, or a code path the owner names for the work'; an amendment to the docspec's own ## Reader or ## Covers names none of its references, so no 'Update the documentation per docspec:<slug>' work item is added, code planning (core.md step 8) matches code paths only, and certification runs its documentation pass only 'per docspec a work item names' (converge/prompts/sprint-review.md:26). The existing documentation keeps addressing the old reader after the sprint that changed the order, and is held to the new ## Reader only when an unrelated change later reaches a reference. Also the reconcile step (core.md out-of-band reviewer) flags only out-of-band edits, so nothing ever brings it back. The story promises: 'whom it is for ... so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; decision out-of-band-documentation-reconciled: 'Keeping the edit must leave the docspec agreeing with the text, or the next builder rewrites the edit away' — the corpus expects text and docspec to agree, yet an approved docspec amendment leaves them disagreeing. Saw: no step in plan-sprint, the build prompt, or certification rewrites documentation to an amended docspec in the amending sprint.

Reviewed the docspec form and the writer and checker that answer to it for a folder kind of documentation. artifact-definitions.md DOCSPEC-DEFINITION: '## Where opens with the path: one file, or a folder, its path ending in /. For a folder, the lines after the path say how its files are laid out.' The builder's DOCUMENTATION-RULE (_sprint/shared.md:108-113) binds the writer to the Reader, Covers, Notes, and Lists only: 'writes its documentation ... for the reader its ## Reader names, covering what its ## Covers names, and keeping its ## Notes. Decide which files under the Where to add, change, or drop.' It never tells the builder to follow the layout lines under ## Where, and certification's documentation pass (converge/prompts/sprint-pass.md:28; catalog C5 in _sprint/shared.md:302) reports only 'each departure from the docspec's ## Reader, ## Covers, or ## Notes'. So an owner's declared layout (in my scratch docspec: 'docs/' then 'One file per command, named after the command.') binds neither the writer nor the check, and the builder is told to decide the files itself. The story promises: 'a way to declare each kind of documentation my project keeps ... so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; concept docspec: 'It says where that documentation lives'. Saw: the layout half of the declared Where is not carried to the writer or the certifier.

brief: story project-spans-folders; drive name project-spans-folders-824844bd

body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md) and the sprint template's completion contract (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md). SKILL.md sprint step 4 says: 'Where review stories prints no slug, or review drive-stack prints unfilled or refuses, skip the drive, and say so in the return with the reason.' Drive step 2, which sprint step 4 runs, says: 'Where the start fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, ... and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds.' The return block is still presented, and the contract (sprint-document.md lines 274-279) requires only that the report 'carries the return block ... the run's find loop ran once, and every defect stands verified, declined, duplicate, or stuck'. So a sprint whose certification drove no story (a transient stack-start failure, or the seeded project.md, whose Drive commands section a fresh true-up leaves unfilled: 'review drive-stack' printed 'unfilled' in a scratch project trued up from the working tree) meets the same contract as a sprint whose every story was driven. By contrast, a review root that fails twice presents no return block, 'so the completion report carries no certification and the completion contract stays open' (SKILL.md line 101): the review not running holds done open, the drive not running does not. The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'; decision drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user's Choice: 'sprint certification each give every story its own driver once per run'; and sprint-document.md step 12 tells the executor certification judges that 'a user gets what every story promises when a driver uses the running product'. Saw: two sprints of one project can both close done, one with every story driven and one with none, and the contract text gives a checker no term that tells them apart. Evidence: scratch run run-3d4a975c8091: 'python3 .ok-planner/bin/review drive-stack' -> 'unfilled' (exit 0) after true-up.

Reviewed the completion contract every sprint carries (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md lines 257-294) against /converge sprint mode. Contract item 1: 'Every corpus matches every delta above, applied verbatim' carries no exception, while item 2 does ('or fail only where sprint certification's return lists the failure as a stuck defect'). The goal rule then says: 'A stuck defect listed in the return, a check that still fails among them, is the owner's to take up, and holds no term of the contract open.' A delta that did not land is a C3 defect the fix loop lands (converge SKILL.md line 105); at fix.max_kickbacks it is stuck, and its backout restores the artifact, since backout.md says 'you back it out as above even where the fix line rule above leaves that file alone'. With a stuck C3 defect, item 1 read as written says not done, and the goal rule read as written says the stuck defect holds no term open, so done. Two checkers following the same contract decide differently. The story promises: 'so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'; decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository: 'A stuck defect the return lists, a check that still fails among them, is the owner's to take up, and holds no term of the contract open.' Saw: item 1 lacks the stuck-defect carve-out item 2 has, so the contract's terms disagree on a sprint with a stuck C3 defect.

Reviewed what sprint certification's return tells the owner (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md line 149). The return's sprint field lists: 'one line per work item and taken improvement, with its entry point ... and whether it works end to end; each docspec whose documentation a documentation pass judged; the behavior changes judged, counted by ruling ...; the stories driven ...; the checks and their final result; the reports sent to the intake'. It names no line for the sprint's corpus deltas, though the alignment pass compares each delta byte for byte (sprint-pass.md) and contract item 1 makes every delta landing a term of done. The deltas appear only where one failed, as a C3 count under fixed. A sprint whose approved content is mostly or only deltas (sprint-document.md step 4: 'Apply a delta no work item implements in a stage of its own') gets a return that says nothing of whether what was approved there was delivered. The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered'. Saw: the return the session writes into the completion report under '# Sprint certification' reports work items, docspecs, rulings, stories, and checks, and is silent on the deltas the owner approved.

body: Reviewed /converge's Loop 2 against the story. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 says: 'A fix task that closed partial with a result starting outside files: waits for the task that held them: its fixer already widened those defects' files, so set its unfinished defects (those still fixing) back to open with kickbacks raised by one'. No fix of those defects was tried or sent back; they only waited on a file another task held. With the seeded fix.max_kickbacks of 2 (review/seed/config.json), a defect deferred once for file contention reaches stuck after a single verifier send-back, has its change backed out, and goes to the owner as a judgment issue. The skill's own premise says otherwise: 'A stuck defect's fix failed twice, so what fixes it is a judgment'. The story promises: 'defects across my product found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'; saw: the text routes to the owner a defect only one fix attempt failed, a question that needs no judgment by the skill's own rule; evidence: SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 (quoted above), Loop 2 step 1 ('Every defect at state open whose kickbacks field has reached config.json fix.max_kickbacks is set to stuck'), seed config 'fix': {'group_size': 4, 'max_kickbacks': 2}.

In a scratch project trued up from the working tree, committed bin/clean (an extensionless shell script), filed a category: defect issue whose problem reads 'bin/clean:main runs rm -rf "$1"/ with no check; ... Accept entry A2.', and ran .ok-planner/bin/review backlog as /converge's backlog step says. It printed {"reports": [], "settled": [{"issue": "clean-empty-arg", "files": [], "left_alone": {}}]} (exit 0): the issue names an existing project file, yet the verb says it names none. scripts/review backlog_entry reads paths with PATH_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[\w./-]+\.\w+") and SITE_PATTERN, both of which need a file extension, so no extensionless file (bin/clean, scripts/review, scripts/tasks, admin/true-up, checks/run here) is ever taken as a file. SKILL.md then has the session add a report saying 'issue <id>: its problem names no file of this tree outside the exclude list', which is false, and the ownership routing for left_alone files never runs for extensionless suite files such as .ok-planner/bin/review. The story promises: defects across the product found and fixed without the owner; saw: a defect issue on an extensionless script reaches the merge agent with a false report and no site, so its fix rests on the merge agent re-deriving what the verb should have found; evidence: the review backlog output quoted above; SKILL.md 'An issue whose problem names no file the run may edit adds no report: the verb lists it under settled, with files: []'.

body: Reviewed /converge sprint (SKILL.md, prompts/sprint-review.md, sprint-pass.md, fix.md, _converge/coding-rules.md) and /plan-sprint's reconcile against the story. Sprint certification judges documentation only for docspecs a work item names: sprint-review.md reads '`documentation`: one pass per docspec a work item names', and class C5 ('the change reached the docspec's references and its documentation did not move') applies only through that pass. No pass, and no script (scripts/review has no docspec matching), checks whether the sprint's change reached the code-path references of a docspec no work item names, which happens wherever a builder or fixer touches a file the code planner's Changes did not list. A fixer cannot move such documentation either: the prose scope rule says documentation is in review only 'where it lies under the ## Where of a docspec ... that a work item of that sprint names ... Anywhere else ... file no finding on it and edit none of it.' The next /plan-sprint does not catch it: its reconcile window is '<closed>..HEAD' with <closed> the sprint's own work commit (plan-sprint SKILL.md Reconcile step 1; archive steps 3-4 stamp 'closed: <the commit's sha>'), so the sprint's own changes are outside every later window. The story promises: 'each change to my product bring[s] the documentation it affects along in the same change, so that the documentation a reader finds at any commit describes the product at that commit'; decision:sprints-write-the-documentation says 'Sprint certification reviews each touched documentation against its docspec and the change'. Saw: a sprint commit can change code a docspec references while that docspec's documentation stays stale, and no step of planning, build, certification, or the next reconcile ever flags it.

Reviewed the sprint build prompt's DOCUMENTATION-RULE (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:115), the text a builder follows to write reference documentation, against the surface intent form in skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md (whose template carries '## Exceptions: Each specific element that departs from its class's rule, named, and which way it departs'). The rule says: 'Where the docspec has a ## Lists section, list every member of each class it names, from the tree as it stands, and no member of another class: the surface intent ... names, under ## Where each class is declared, the files that declare each class's members; read each declaring file whole.' It never tells the builder to read the intent's ## Exceptions or to leave out a member the intent makes internal by exception. A builder that follows it lists every member the declaring file holds, so an element the owner named internal (e.g. intent 'Every CLI verb is public' + exception 'The verb debug-dump is internal', declaring file src/cli.py) is written into the reference. The story promises: the reference names no element I kept internal. Saw: the rule's only exclusion is 'no member of another class'; internal exceptions of a listed class are listed.

Reviewed sprint certification's fix loop (converge SKILL.md sprint mode and Loop 2, prompts/fix.md, prompts/verify.md). The documentation pass reads once before any fix ('The review reads once, and its reading is the run's scope: nothing found later joins the list'; 'Neither loop re-hunts code a fix changed'). fix.md tells the fixer 'Change nothing the defect does not need: no rename, no reshaping, no fix of something you happened to notice' and says nothing about bringing documentation along when a fix changes behavior a named docspec's documentation describes; verify.md checks 'the change, and only the change' against the accept list and release boundaries, never against a docspec. So a certification fix that changes an observable behavior (a flag, a message, an output format) lands in the sprint's commit while the documentation still describes the pre-fix behavior, and the next /plan-sprint reconcile window starts after that commit, so nothing catches it. The story promises: the documentation a reader finds at any commit describes the product at that commit, each change bringing its documentation along in the same change. Saw: no instruction in the fix or verify prompts moves documentation with a certification fix, and no later step re-checks it.

Reviewed the sprint build prompt's DOCUMENTATION-RULE (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:115) against the surface intent's form (class rules with named exceptions, skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md SURFACE-INTENT-DEFINITION). The rule says 'list every member of each class it names, from the tree as it stands, and no member of another class'. An element the intent's ## Exceptions makes public out of a class that is internal by default belongs to a class no reference docspec can name under ## Lists (Lists names 'one class of public surface per bullet'), and the rule forbids listing it ('no member of another class'). The story promises: the reference names every element I made public. Saw: an element made public by a named exception has no path into the reference; the builder text excludes it explicitly.

Reviewed /converge in drive, analysis, and defects mode. These runs fix product code and end with an offer to commit the fixes (SKILL.md 'End it with one offer, to archive and commit the run: the fixes, ...'). The prose scope rule they carry (_converge/coding-rules.md PROSE-SCOPE-RULE) says of documentation: 'Anywhere else, and in a run that certifies no sprint, file no finding on it and edit none of it.' So a converge fix that changes behavior a docspec's code-path references cover is committed with that documentation describing the old behavior; /plan-sprint's reconcile flags it only at the next planning session ('Code or a corpus artifact a docspec references, changed outside a sprint'), and the commits in between show stale documentation. The story promises: 'each change to my product bring the documentation it affects along in the same change, so that the documentation a reader finds at any commit describes the product at that commit.' decision:sprints-write-the-documentation chooses 'Of the suite's runs, only a sprint writes a project's documentation', so the decision and the story's 'at any commit' disagree for converge's own commits; the owner decides which stands. Saw: converge-run commits leave referenced documentation behind until a later sprint.

Reviewed sprint certification's documentation pass (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/sprint-pass.md:28) and class C5 (skills/_sprint/shared.md:302). The pass says: 'list every member of each class it names from the files the surface intent names as declaring that class, reading each whole, and report each member the documentation omits.' C5 names 'a member of a class its ## Lists names is missing', a false sentence, a Reader/Covers/Notes departure, or unmoved documentation. Neither tells the pass to report an element the documentation names that the intent keeps internal: a member of a listed class the intent's ## Exceptions makes internal, or a member of a class that is not public. So a reference that lists an internal element passes certification. decision surface-members-listed-at-need: 'sprint certification lists them again to check that the documentation misses none' covers completeness only. The story promises: the reference names no element I kept internal, so a reader depends on nothing else. Saw: no check in certification refuses an internal element in a reference.

Reviewed the documentation pass (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/sprint-pass.md:28): it lists 'every member of each class it names from the files the surface intent names as declaring that class' and reports omissions. An element the surface intent's ## Exceptions makes public out of an internal-by-default class is in no class the docspec's ## Lists names, so the pass never lists it and never reports its absence, and the builder rule (skills/_sprint/shared.md:115, 'no member of another class') guarantees it is absent. The story promises: the reference names every element I made public. Saw: certification's completeness check reads class membership only and misses public exceptions.

Reviewed /plan-sprint's documentation match (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md:105: 'a docspec whose references include a corpus artifact a work item or delta names, or a code path the owner names for the work, is touched'), code planning's step 8 (skills/plan-sprint/core.md:296: 'a docspec is reached where a path under Changes falls under one of its code-path references'), and the docspec index catalog-toc writes (ran plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/catalog-toc on a scratch project with a reference docspec whose ## Lists names 'CLI verbs': the row reads '-  — where: docs/cli.md; references: ', no Lists). A reference docspec is matched only by its ## References; neither its ## Lists classes, their declaring files under the surface intent's '## Where each class is declared', nor a surface intent delta reaches it. So a sprint that adds a member to a listed class in a declaring file the References omit, or whose surface intent delta moves an element to internal or public by exception, gets no 'Update the documentation per docspec:<slug>' work item, and certification has no documentation pass for it (sprint-review.md:26: 'A sprint whose work items name no docspec has no documentation pass'). The docspec definition and the compliance reviewer (skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md, Docspec form) never require a reference docspec's References to cover its Lists' declaring files or the surface intent. The story promises: the reference names every element I made public and none I kept internal. Saw: a change to the public surface can leave the reference stale with nothing in planning or certification that notices.

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md against the story, and ran the review verbs it calls in a scratch repo (project root repo/app, declared folder ../lib, .ok-planner/config.json {"folders":["../missing","../lib"]}, a stale entry beside a valid one). The review tool drops every declared folder, the valid ../lib included, and exits 0 with a note on stderr only: 'review: .ok-planner/config.json is malformed, so the review reads the project root alone; run /ok, which repairs it: folders[0] "../missing" is not an existing directory'. That note comes from review files, review changed, review areas, and review checks (the filed check task's command became 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline .ok-planner/config.json', dropping ../lib/util.py; areas fell from 8 to 6 with no ../lib area). The skill never tells the session to relay that note: SKILL.md step 1 says only 'Say the run's shape in one line before it starts ... the count of changed files ...' and defines the changed files as 'every file added, changed, or deleted since the base under the project root and its declared folders', and analysis step 1 relays only the surface-intent note ('the verb says so on stderr and the run hunts file areas alone; say so in the return'). No line of the return block names it either. A session following the text runs analysis or sprint certification over the root alone and reports its hunt and its checks as passing, with nothing telling the owner that the code under the declared folders was skipped. The story promises: 'a way to declare every folder my project owns, so that no check the suite runs over my project misses code I own.' Saw: with one stale folders entry, the review loop misses every declared folder and the skill's return stays silent about it. Evidence: review files printed only '.ok-planner/config.json', '.ok-planner/review/config.json', 'main.py' (exit 0) where the valid config printed '../lib/util.py' as well; review checks filed 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline .ok-planner/config.json' (exit 0) where the valid config filed 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline ../lib/util.py .ok-planner/config.json'.

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md (sections 6, 9, 10, 12) and core.md {{CODE-PLANNER-PROMPT}} for a feature-work sprint. The relevance pass runs once, at Resolve, against the draft as it stood then. After it, the work changes three ways and none of them goes back through it. (1) SKILL.md section 10: 'Where a planner's Docspecs: line names a docspec no work item names, add its Update the documentation per docspec:<slug> work item as a call'. This adds a new work item. (2) Section 10, kickback: 'it goes back to the draft, where you reshape it into the feature, script, or seed asset ... as a call'. This reshapes a work item. (3) Section 12: 'An owner's change at approval re-runs the steps it touches: a delta goes through the compliance review, and a work item goes through code planning and the notes review'. Resolve and the relevance pass are left out. Also, core.md {{CODE-PLANNER-PROMPT}} lists its inputs as the sprint, accept.md, project.md, the corpus, and docspec.md. It never gets the intake. Yet step 6 tells it to 'Make every other determined choice yourself and list it under Calls ... a field name, an error path, a retry, what an unlisted surface shows'. {{OWNER-QUESTION-TEST}} sends a call to the owner only for a promise change, a boundary break, or a split reading of a ruling. A call that answers an open issue meets none of the three. So a call, a new work item, or a reshaped one can answer an unruled issue that the relevance pass judged INDEPENDENT against the earlier draft, and the owner is never asked. The story promises: 'so that any executor can realize my intent without re-deriving it or deciding my open questions for me'. decision:relevance-scoped-queue-gate says: 'building over a bearing issue decides it silently' and 'When you cannot tell, it answers that the issue bears.' Saw: no step after Resolve checks the work it adds or changes against the unruled open issues. evidence: the quoted SKILL.md lines in sections 10 and 12, and the code planner's Inputs block in core.md, which names no intake.

Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md and sprint-document.md. Section 5 (Draft): 'Write the sprint to .ok-planner/sprints/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md from {{SPRINT-DOCUMENT-TEMPLATE}}'. The template copies in the fixed 'How to execute this sprint' and 'Completion contract' sections. Sign-off (7), code planning (9), the owner's judgments (10), and Approval (12) all come after this write. Section 12 says: 'It is not final until the owner approves.' But neither the template nor the skill writes any mark that tells an approved sprint from a draft. Section 6 covers a session that dies before approval only for the intake: it 'leaves the promoted-in-spirit issues open with their rulings preserved — the correct state'. Nothing removes or marks the draft file left in .ok-planner/sprints/. Its Implementation notes may still read 'pending'. Nothing downstream refuses it either. I grepped converge/SKILL.md, converge/prompts/sprint-review.md, and _tasks/drain.md: none checks approval or 'pending'. In the scratch project, '.ok-planner/bin/issues promote <id> --sprint <file>' also took a file holding only a title and an Intent heading: 'promoted pas-ruled into 2026-10-17-plan-a-sprint-824844bd.md', exit 0. The story promises: 'a signed-off, self-sufficient sprint, so that any executor can realize my intent'. Saw: an executor that reads the file, such as /goal on the path or '/converge sprint <path>', cannot tell a sprint the owner signed off from an abandoned draft, and runs whatever stands in it. evidence: the quoted lines from SKILL.md sections 5, 6, and 12. The grep of the downstream skills for an approval check found none. The promote output is from the scratch run.

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-version/SKILL.md, the session-start hook it reads (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/hooks/session-start), and plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md; the story promises: 'a way to see which plugin version governs my current session beside the version this project's vendored layer carries, so that version drift is visible'; saw: the skill's 'Plugin version (governing this session)' is never a plugin's version. Step 1 reads it from the line 'ok-planner vX.Y.Z is materialized in this project', which the vendored hook emits from its own true-up stamp ('context="ok-planner v{{OK_PLANNER_VERSION}} is materialized in this project..."' in scripts/hooks/session-start), or from the 'Materialized by ok-planner v<X.Y.Z>' line of a vendored rules file. The skill itself says so: 'Both sources are written by the vendored layer the session started with, so the value equals the vendored stamp (step 2) unless an /ok run trued up the project during this session.' So both reported numbers are vendored-layer stamps, and the skill never reads the installed ok plugin's version (the front door that carries the ok-planner family; plugins/ok/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, readable through 'claude plugin list --json', which /ok step 1 already uses). The common drift is invisible: the user-scoped ok plugin is updated to a newer version (by /ok in another project, since plugin content is per machine) while this project stays vendored at the old one; /ok-version then prints the same version on both lines. The suite elsewhere names exactly that gap as the drift signal: /ok's report says '**carried** is the suite version the resolved payload carries ... **vendored in project** is the version the vendored layer's stamps record here ... The gap between the two columns is the useful signal'. The skill's description also names an 'ok-planner plugin version', but ok-planner is a family the ok plugin carries, not a plugin. evidence: SKILL.md step 1 and step 4 lines '- **Plugin version (governing this session):** <X.Y.Z or unknown>' and '- **Vendored layer (this project's stamp):** <X.Y.Z or —>', both sourced from vendored stamps.

body: Reviewed /plan-sprint Draft (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md:107), the one place planning settles new surface. Diverging line: "The predictive classification test. Where `.ok-planner/surface/surface.md` exists, check each piece of new user-facing surface the work introduces ... against the surface intent". Where the file does not exist the session skips the test entirely, and no step of the skill (nor artifact-definitions.md, core.md, sprint-document.md) tells the session to draft a `### New surface intent` delta or to ask the owner about each new element. Nothing else creates the file now that /audit is retired: a fresh true-up places none, and this repository itself has none. Evidence: stack up run-ca895d6c52e3 (git init scratch project), `bash plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up` from it exited 0 with "Trued up ok-planner at .../project (v26.0.0).", and `ls .ok-planner/surface` printed "ls: .ok-planner/surface: No such file or directory"; at the repo root `ls -la .ok-planner/surface/` printed the same; `grep -rn "New surface intent" plugins/` finds only the delta form in artifact-definitions.md:263, no instruction to draft one. So in every project without an intent, each new command, route, or env var a sprint adds ships without the owner deciding whether it is public. The story promises: "a way to decide whether each new user-facing element of my project is public before it ships, so that no element becomes part of my public surface unless I chose it." Decision surface-intent-changed-by-sprints: "Planning checks every new command, route, or other user-facing element the drafted work introduces against the intent. An element no rule of the intent claims is a question to the owner, and the answer becomes a surface-intent delta in the same sprint." With no intent, no rule claims any element, so every new element should be a question and the answer a `### New surface intent` delta.

Reviewed the predictive classification test, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md:107. Diverging sentence: "Stories carry the public-by-construction prior: a story's capability is something a user reaches, so its surface is public unless the owner says otherwise, and only genuine ambiguity reaches the owner." It follows "An unclaimed one is one prose question to the owner", and overrides it: an element no rule of the intent claims, but that realizes a story, is taken as public by the session without a question, and the paragraph says no delta is drafted for it (the delta is drafted only "on the answer"), so the intent still claims nothing for the element after the sprint ships it. The story promises: "so that no element becomes part of my public surface unless I chose it." Decision surface-intent-changed-by-sprints, Choice: "An element no rule of the intent claims is a question to the owner, and the answer becomes a surface-intent delta in the same sprint." The prior lets the session, not the owner, choose, and leaves the element unclassified for the next reader of the intent.

Reviewed where else a new user-facing element can enter a sprint: code planning (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/core.md, CODE-PLANNER-PROMPT), the owner question test (skills/_sprint/shared.md, OWNER-QUESTION-TEST), the build prompt (shared.md, SPRINT-BUILD-PROMPT) and certification (converge/prompts/sprint-pass.md, sprint-review.md). The classification test runs only at Draft (SKILL.md:107), against what the draft names. The code planner names new definitions, flags, and configuration keys ("2. List the changes: each definition, file, configuration key, schema, or stored layout the outcome needs added") but its Inputs never include `.ok-planner/surface/surface.md`, and it settles the rest itself: "6. Make every other determined choice yourself and list it under **Calls** ... what an unlisted surface shows." The owner question test sends a question to the owner only for a promise change, a boundary break, or a split ruling, and says "Every other question is a call"; it has no clause for an element no intent rule claims. A builder that adds an element records it as a call or an "unlisted behavior change", and certification "judges each call against the accept list ... it asks the owner about none"; neither sprint-pass.md nor sprint-review.md checks new elements against the intent (grep for public/user-facing/surface intent finds only the C3 delta comparison and the docspec Lists pass). So a verb, flag, route, or env var first named at code planning or build ships classified by nobody. The story promises: "a way to decide whether each new user-facing element of my project is public before it ships". Decision surface-intent-changed-by-sprints: "Planning checks every new command, route, or other user-facing element the drafted work introduces against the intent." Rationale: "Checking each new element there settles its class before it ships".

body: B113 widens Loop 2 step 4's refile rule to fix tasks that close blocked or disputed: 'A fix task that closes blocked or disputed, or partial with any other result, is refiled once with tasks refile <task> and drained'. review fixes chains the fix tasks of one overlapping group behind each other with --after, and tasks::ready treats a dependency as met once it is CLOSED, whatever its outcome (scripts/tasks:566-571: 'if d is None or d["state"] != CLOSED: return False'). tasks::cmd_refile files the refile with after=[] (scripts/tasks:815 'spec["after"] = args.after or []'). So when a chained fix task closes blocked or disputed, its successor (filed after it because their files overlap) becomes ready at once, and the refile the step files runs beside it: two fixers edit the same overlapping files in one round, a second writer between two steps of one change (A1), and each fixer's staged paths and the verifier's before-blobs no longer describe one fixer's hunks. Trigger: a group of two or more overlapping fix tasks whose first closes blocked or disputed. Fix: refile with --after naming the open successors, or hold the successor (the step names no ordering). Scope: reached; the same hazard already stood at the base for a partial close, and the change extends it to two more outcomes.

body: In a scratch project (true-up of the working tree, dashboard page built from the tree's source), I seeded an upstream issue rule-on-the-whole-intake-q9 routed as triage-issues/SKILL.md's upstream row says (route upstream, three options: a workaround, a filing upstream, or both, and a recommended ruling 'File the draft with the ok suite.'), then on the dashboard page opened 'needs ruling', pressed j and then a (Accept the recommendation). The page recorded the ruling 'File the draft with the ok suite.' signed 'ruled by Rule Owner A'; issues show prints 'Ruling (2026-10-17T09:21:19Z): File the draft with the ok suite.'. I then read how the next /plan-sprint treats that ruled issue. plan-sprint/SKILL.md, Frame, 'Set the upstream issues apart': 'A ruling that names where the owner filed it, and asks for no workaround, is a filing upstream: record it now ... A ruling that names a workaround rides the sweep like any ruled issue ... A ruling that names neither cannot be understood: ask the owner about it, as above.' An accepted filing recommendation names an intent to file, not where it was filed, and no workaround, so Frame asks the owner about it again. The story promises: 'As a project owner, I want a way to rule on every open judgment issue in one sitting, so that my next planning session starts with no question left unanswered.' Saw: a ruling the product itself offers as one key (accept triage's recommended filing) on every upstream issue triage recommends filing reaches the next planning session as a question, so the session does not start with every question answered. The ruling the page offers and the ruling Frame can act on disagree: either Frame takes an accepted 'file upstream' ruling as the owner's answer (walking only the act of filing, or closing once a filing is named), or the page and the upstream recommendation tell the owner the ruling must name where it was filed. A ruling typed by hand that names a workaround ('file it upstream and pin the library meanwhile', issue rule-on-the-whole-intake-up) does ride the sweep. Evidence: page text after a: 'RULING / File the draft with the ok suite. / ruled by Rule Owner A2026-10-17T09:21:19Z · Withdraw ruling / UPSTREAM ISSUE / The suite hook times out after 5 s.'

body: Reviewed the sprint execution boilerplate (sprint-document.md step 13) and drove its commands in a scratch project: recorded build calls (kind call, fork, noticed) in a sprint run and certification calls (declined defect, rejected report, not-owed failure, unlisted call) in a converge ledger, re-rendered with 'tasks --file <run> render --certification <ledger>' (exit 0; all 8 rows shown, cert: rows included), then filed the owner's veto of row cert:i1 exactly as step 13 says. The seeing half holds. The overturning half does not bind. Step 13 says: 'For each vetoed row, file one issue with .ok-planner/bin/issues file --from - ... kind human, category product-intent, its problem the row and the owner's words, for the next /plan-sprint.' The owner's words go into problem, never into a ruling: 'issues list --json' after filing printed 'veto-calls-made-in-my-absence-cert-i1 open None True' (state open, ruling None, waiting True). An unruled issue goes to /triage-issues, whose triage prompt sorts 'a problem whose one option fixes a code site' as a defect claim and routes it 'retired' 'Where no entry covers a harm the code causes today'; a vetoed decline or rejection is exactly a harm a fixer or merge agent already judged the accept list leaves standing, so triage closes the owner's veto as retired. Routed question instead, it gets a recommended ruling that 'Silence accepts' (ok-planner-cheatsheet), so the next /plan-sprint rides the agent's recommendation, not the owner's veto, unless the owner rules a second time. The artifact definitions say /plan-sprint transcribes 'a decision a person gives live, under that person's name' with 'issues rule', and triage 'never closes a record that carries a ruling'; step 13 takes the owner's live veto and records no ruling. The story promises: 'a way to see every call made while I was away, so that I can overturn one I disagree with.' The completion-report concept: 'it puts every call before the owner at once, so the owner can veto any call they disagree with.' Saw: a veto filed per step 13 is an unruled product-intent issue that an agent may retire or answer, or carry with the agent's own recommended ruling, so the overturn does not stand on the owner's word.

Reviewed /converge's return in drive, analysis, and defects mode (SKILL.md 'The return') against its calls config, and drove 'tasks calls' on a ledger carrying converge's 'tasks config set calls' selectors in a scratch project: it printed one row per declined defect, rejected report, not-owed failure, and unlisted call (exit 0), so the owner sees the calls. The skill gives the owner no way to overturn one. SKILL.md says the return lists 'calls, in drive, analysis, and defects mode: what tasks calls prints, one row per decline, duplicate, not-owed or rejected failure, and rejected report', then: 'In drive, analysis, and defects mode, the block is the whole report: it asks the owner nothing ... End it with one offer, to archive and commit the run.' The owner list files only 'a decline or duplicate no verifier checked' (owner-list.md); a verified decline, a rejected report, and a not-owed failure reach no issue, and the session neither asks which rows the owner vetoes nor names how to overturn one, unlike sprint mode, whose boilerplate step 13 asks 'which rows, if any, the owner vetoes' and files an issue per vetoed row. The story promises: 'a way to see every call made while I was away, so that I can overturn one I disagree with.' Saw: after an unattended drive, analysis, or defects run, a call the owner disagrees with (a fixer's verified decline of a real defect) is shown once in the return and then committed with the run; nothing the skill offers turns the owner's disagreement into an issue or a fix.

The same happened on upgrade: a project laid out by the v26.0.0 core (git archive v26.0.0) with an uncommitted line 'B-UNCOMMITTED-RULES-EDIT' appended to its stamped .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md, trued up with --go-ahead 02387b6cb288. The story promises: upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote; whole-file-ownership says 'so true-up never discards uncommitted work', and the removal rule archives a suite file with an uncommitted change rather than removing it. Saw: diagnose listed the overwrite as a non-destructive step, so the plan carried no question, and the true-up overwrote the file. The uncommitted lines are in no file of the tree, the archive, or HEAD, and no report line names them. Evidence: diagnose printed 'DRIFT: stale: .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md differs from the carried v26.0.0 rendering' and 'PLAN: 1 step(s), 0 destructive; plan 8c2a3d05b87e'; the bare true-up exited 0 with 'materialized: 1 files under .ok-planner/ and .claude/ (v26.0.0)' and 'Trued up ok-planner at .../c (v26.0.0).'; afterwards grep -rl C-UNCOMMITTED-OWNER-RULE over the tree found nothing, git grep over HEAD found nothing, and git status was clean. In the upgraded v26 project, a scan of every owner marker found every one kept but 'B-UNCOMMITTED-RULES-EDIT (HEAD: )', which was gone. An unstamped vendored prompt (.claude/skills/converge/prompts/fix.md) given the same kind of edit was archived under a DESTRUCTIVE step, so only stamped files lose the edit. The decisions call a stamped file suite-owned, so a fix may need the owner to choose: treat a stamped suite file with an uncommitted or staged-only change as destructive (archive a copy first), or accept the loss.

Reviewed plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md, admin/ADMINISTRATION.md, and the admin/true-up core it drives, and ran the core against scratch projects. SKILL.md step 4.4 says 'A plan with no destructive step needs no question', and its Boundaries say 'Writes nothing the owner has not let proceed'. ADMINISTRATION.md defines DRIFT as 'a step that destroys nothing: writing or regenerating a suite file', and the core classes a rewrite of a stamped suite file as DRIFT whatever its git state. So a session that follows /ok overwrites an uncommitted owner edit in a stamped suite file (such as .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md) with no question, no archive, and no report line. The story promises: upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote; whole-file-ownership says 'so true-up never discards uncommitted work', and the removal rule ('Every other file the plan would remove — one with an uncommitted or staged-only change ... — moves to the archive instead') protects the same file when it is removed but not when it is rewritten. body: In a scratch project bootstrapped by the working tree's core (bash plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up, exit 0) and committed, I appended four lines ('## My project rule' / 'C-UNCOMMITTED-OWNER-RULE: always name the widget.') to the stamped .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md without committing, ran diagnose, then the bare true-up. The same happened on upgrade: a project laid out by the v26.0.0 core (git archive v26.0.0) with an uncommitted line 'B-UNCOMMITTED-RULES-EDIT' appended to its stamped .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md, trued up with --go-ahead 02387b6cb288. The story promises: upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote; whole-file-ownership says 'so true-up never discards uncommitted work', and the removal rule archives a suite file with an uncommitted change rather than removing it. Saw: diagnose listed the overwrite as a non-destructive step, so the plan carried no question, and the true-up overwrote the file. The uncommitted lines are in no file of the tree, the archive, or HEAD, and no report line names them. Evidence: diagnose printed 'DRIFT: stale: .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md differs from the carried v26.0.0 rendering' and 'PLAN: 1 step(s), 0 destructive; plan 8c2a3d05b87e'; the bare true-up exited 0 with 'materialized: 1 files under .ok-planner/ and .claude/ (v26.0.0)' and 'Trued up ok-planner at .../c (v26.0.0).'; afterwards grep -rl C-UNCOMMITTED-OWNER-RULE over the tree found nothing, git grep over HEAD found nothing, and git status was clean. In the upgraded v26 project, a scan of every owner marker found every one kept but 'B-UNCOMMITTED-RULES-EDIT (HEAD: )', which was gone. An unstamped vendored prompt (.claude/skills/converge/prompts/fix.md) given the same kind of edit was archived under a DESTRUCTIVE step, so only stamped files lose the edit. The decisions call a stamped file suite-owned, so a fix may need the owner to choose: treat a stamped suite file with an uncommitted or staged-only change as destructive (archive a copy first), or accept the loss.
note: two readings: the story true-up-project-estate promises "upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote", which covers uncommitted lines an owner appended to a stamped suite file; the decision whole-file-ownership Choice says "True-up rewrites a suite-owned file that carries its stamp or its fixed content with no question" and confines "so true-up never discards uncommitted work" to removals, and ADMINISTRATION.md classes as destructive only a rewrite of "every file but a suite-owned file that still carries its stamp", so the core and /ok behave as the Choice states; the story sentence and the Choice sentence each rest one reading. body: Reviewed plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md, admin/ADMINISTRATION.md, and the admin/true-up core it drives, and ran the core against scratch projects. SKILL.md step 4.4 says 'A plan with no destructive step needs no question', and its Boundaries say 'Writes nothing the owner has not let proceed'. ADMINISTRATION.md defines DRIFT as 'a step that destroys nothing: writing or regenerating a suite file', and the core classes a rewrite of a stamped suite file as DRIFT whatever its git state. So a session that follows /ok overwrites an uncommitted owner edit in a stamped suite file (such as .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md) with no question, no archive, and no report line. The story promises: upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote; whole-file-ownership says 'so true-up never discards uncommitted work', and the removal rule ('Every other file the plan would remove — one with an uncommitted or staged-only change ... — moves to the archive instead') protects the same file when it is removed but not when it is rewritten. In a current project, 'PLAN: 1 step(s), 0 destructive' was followed by a bare true-up (exit 0) that discarded 4 uncommitted lines; the core's own flow, which /ok follows, asked nothing. body: B113 widens Loop 2 step 4's refile rule to fix tasks that close blocked or disputed: 'A fix task that closes blocked or disputed, or partial with any other result, is refiled once with tasks refile <task> and drained'. review fixes chains the fix tasks of one overlapping group behind each other with --after, and tasks::ready treats a dependency as met once it is CLOSED, whatever its outcome (scripts/tasks:566-571: 'if d is None or d["state"] != CLOSED: return False'). tasks::cmd_refile files the refile with after=[] (scripts/tasks:815 'spec["after"] = args.after or []'). So when a chained fix task closes blocked or disputed, its successor (filed after it because their files overlap) becomes ready at once, and the refile the step files runs beside it: two fixers edit the same overlapping files in one round, a second writer between two steps of one change (A1), and each fixer's staged paths and the verifier's before-blobs no longer describe one fixer's hunks. Trigger: a group of two or more overlapping fix tasks whose first closes blocked or disputed. Fix: refile with --after naming the open successors, or hold the successor (the step names no ordering). Scope: reached; the same hazard already stood at the base for a partial close, and the change extends it to two more outcomes.

Reviewed /plan-sprint (SKILL.md Draft, core.md code planner step 8), the sprint build prompt's documentation rule (_sprint/shared.md), and certification's documentation pass (converge/prompts/sprint-review.md, sprint-pass.md) for an owner declaring a new kind of documentation through a '### New docspec: <slug>' delta. The documentation match reads only the live index: SKILL.md:105 'Where .ok-planner/docspec/ exists, read the docspec index at .ok-planner/docspec.md ... a docspec whose references include a corpus artifact a work item or delta names, or a code path the owner names for the work, is touched. Add one work item per touched docspec'. A docspec drafted as a delta in this same sprint is not in the index (catalog-toc regenerates it only when the delta is applied at execution), and nothing says a New docspec delta itself makes its docspec touched; code planning (core.md step 8) matches only 'a path under Changes falls under one of its code-path references' against the same index. The builder writes documentation only where 'A builder whose work item names docspec:<slug>' (_sprint/shared.md DOCUMENTATION-RULE), and certification files a documentation pass only 'per docspec a work item names' (sprint-review.md:26). So the sprint that declares the new docspec applies the file and writes none of the documentation it orders, and no later run writes it until some unrelated change happens to reach one of its references. The story promises: 'a way to declare each kind of documentation my project keeps ... so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; decision sprints-write-the-documentation: 'adds one work item for each docspec the work touches'. Saw: a newly declared kind of documentation has no writer in the declaring sprint, and certification never checks it against the order. Scripts side checked: in a scratch project, catalog-toc listed a new docspec ('- `ddoc-readme` — where: README.md; references: story:ddoc-export, `src/cli.py`') only after the file was written.

Reviewed /plan-sprint for an owner who changes whom an existing kind of documentation is for (or what it covers) through an '### Amend docspec: <slug>' delta. The documentation match (SKILL.md:105) touches a docspec only where 'its references include a corpus artifact a work item or delta names, or a code path the owner names for the work'; an amendment to the docspec's own ## Reader or ## Covers names none of its references, so no 'Update the documentation per docspec:<slug>' work item is added, code planning (core.md step 8) matches code paths only, and certification runs its documentation pass only 'per docspec a work item names' (converge/prompts/sprint-review.md:26). Also the reconcile step (core.md out-of-band reviewer) flags only out-of-band edits, so nothing ever brings it back. The story promises: 'whom it is for ... so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; decision out-of-band-documentation-reconciled: 'Keeping the edit must leave the docspec agreeing with the text, or the next builder rewrites the edit away' — the corpus expects text and docspec to agree, yet an approved docspec amendment leaves them disagreeing. Saw: no step in plan-sprint, the build prompt, or certification rewrites documentation to an amended docspec in the amending sprint.

Reviewed the docspec form and the writer and checker that answer to it for a folder kind of documentation. artifact-definitions.md DOCSPEC-DEFINITION: '## Where opens with the path: one file, or a folder, its path ending in /. For a folder, the lines after the path say how its files are laid out.' The builder's DOCUMENTATION-RULE (_sprint/shared.md:108-113) binds the writer to the Reader, Covers, Notes, and Lists only: 'writes its documentation ... for the reader its ## Reader names, covering what its ## Covers names, and keeping its ## Notes. So an owner's declared layout (in my scratch docspec: 'docs/' then 'One file per command, named after the command.') binds neither the writer nor the check, and the builder is told to decide the files itself. Saw: the layout half of the declared Where is not carried to the writer or the certifier.

Reviewed /converge sprint (SKILL.md, prompts/sprint-review.md, sprint-pass.md, fix.md, _converge/coding-rules.md) and /plan-sprint's reconcile against the story. Sprint certification judges documentation only for docspecs a work item names: sprint-review.md reads '`documentation`: one pass per docspec a work item names', and class C5 ('the change reached the docspec's references and its documentation did not move') applies only through that pass. No pass, and no script (scripts/review has no docspec matching), checks whether the sprint's change reached the code-path references of a docspec no work item names, which happens wherever a builder or fixer touches a file the code planner's Changes did not list. A fixer cannot move such documentation either: the prose scope rule says documentation is in review only 'where it lies under the ## Where of a docspec ... that a work item of that sprint names ... Anywhere else ... file no finding on it and edit none of it.' The next /plan-sprint does not catch it: its reconcile window is '<closed>..HEAD' with <closed> the sprint's own work commit (plan-sprint SKILL.md Reconcile step 1; archive steps 3-4 stamp 'closed: <the commit's sha>'), so the sprint's own changes are outside every later window. The story promises: 'each change to my product bring[s] the documentation it affects along in the same change, so that the documentation a reader finds at any commit describes the product at that commit'; decision:sprints-write-the-documentation says 'Sprint certification reviews each touched documentation against its docspec and the change'. Saw: a sprint commit can change code a docspec references while that docspec's documentation stays stale, and no step of planning, build, certification, or the next reconcile ever flags it.

Reviewed sprint certification's fix loop (converge SKILL.md sprint mode and Loop 2, prompts/fix.md, prompts/verify.md). The documentation pass reads once before any fix ('The review reads once, and its reading is the run's scope: nothing found later joins the list'; 'Neither loop re-hunts code a fix changed'). fix.md tells the fixer 'Change nothing the defect does not need: no rename, no reshaping, no fix of something you happened to notice' and says nothing about bringing documentation along when a fix changes behavior a named docspec's documentation describes; verify.md checks 'the change, and only the change' against the accept list and release boundaries, never against a docspec. So a certification fix that changes an observable behavior (a flag, a message, an output format) lands in the sprint's commit while the documentation still describes the pre-fix behavior, and the next /plan-sprint reconcile window starts after that commit, so nothing catches it. The story promises: the documentation a reader finds at any commit describes the product at that commit, each change bringing its documentation along in the same change. Saw: no instruction in the fix or verify prompts moves documentation with a certification fix, and no later step re-checks it.

body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md) and the sprint template's completion contract (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md). SKILL.md sprint step 4 says: 'Where review stories prints no slug, or review drive-stack prints unfilled or refuses, skip the drive, and say so in the return with the reason.' Drive step 2, which sprint step 4 runs, says: 'Where the start fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, ... and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds.' The return block is still presented, and the contract (sprint-document.md lines 274-279) requires only that the report 'carries the return block ... the run's find loop ran once, and every defect stands verified, declined, duplicate, or stuck'. So a sprint whose certification drove no story (a transient stack-start failure, or the seeded project.md, whose Drive commands section a fresh true-up leaves unfilled: 'review drive-stack' printed 'unfilled' in a scratch project trued up from the working tree) meets the same contract as a sprint whose every story was driven. By contrast, a review root that fails twice presents no return block, 'so the completion report carries no certification and the completion contract stays open' (SKILL.md line 101): the review not running holds done open, the drive not running does not. The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'; decision drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user's Choice: 'sprint certification each give every story its own driver once per run'; and sprint-document.md step 12 tells the executor certification judges that 'a user gets what every story promises when a driver uses the running product'. Saw: two sprints of one project can both close done, one with every story driven and one with none, and the contract text gives a checker no term that tells them apart. Evidence: scratch run run-3d4a975c8091: 'python3 .ok-planner/bin/review drive-stack' -> 'unfilled' (exit 0) after true-up.

(SKILL.md:104), and the completion contract item 3 is met by a return whose find loop ran, so a sprint whose certification drove no story closes done like one whose every story was driven, against decision drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user ('sprint certification each give every story its own driver once per run') and story certify-completion ('so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'); evidence: a fresh true-up's project.md makes 'review drive-stack' print 'unfilled' (driver's scratch run run-3d4a975c8091); outside the sprint: the step reads the same at 89b51cf (base line 102), and the contract's item 3 is unchanged; WI 16's review-root rule sits beside it and does not reach the drive's skip

body: Reviewed /converge's Loop 2 against the story. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 says: 'A fix task that closed partial with a result starting outside files: waits for the task that held them: its fixer already widened those defects' files, so set its unfinished defects (those still fixing) back to open with kickbacks raised by one'. No fix of those defects was tried or sent back; they only waited on a file another task held. With the seeded fix.max_kickbacks of 2 (review/seed/config.json), a defect deferred once for file contention reaches stuck after a single verifier send-back, has its change backed out, and goes to the owner as a judgment issue. The skill's own premise says otherwise: 'A stuck defect's fix failed twice, so what fixes it is a judgment'. The story promises: 'defects across my product found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'; saw: the text routes to the owner a defect only one fix attempt failed, a question that needs no judgment by the skill's own rule; evidence: SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 (quoted above), Loop 2 step 1 ('Every defect at state open whose kickbacks field has reached config.json fix.max_kickbacks is set to stuck'), seed config 'fix': {'group_size': 4, 'max_kickbacks': 2}.

body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree, committed bin/clean (an extensionless shell script), filed a category: defect issue whose problem reads 'bin/clean:main runs rm -rf "$1"/ with no check; ... Accept entry A2.', and ran .ok-planner/bin/review backlog as /converge's backlog step says. It printed {"reports": [], "settled": [{"issue": "clean-empty-arg", "files": [], "left_alone": {}}]} (exit 0): the issue names an existing project file, yet the verb says it names none. scripts/review backlog_entry reads paths with PATH_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[\w./-]+\.\w+") and SITE_PATTERN, both of which need a file extension, so no extensionless file (bin/clean, scripts/review, scripts/tasks, admin/true-up, checks/run here) is ever taken as a file. SKILL.md then has the session add a report saying 'issue <id>: its problem names no file of this tree outside the exclude list', which is false, and the ownership routing for left_alone files never runs for extensionless suite files such as .ok-planner/bin/review. The story promises: defects across the product found and fixed without the owner; saw: a defect issue on an extensionless script reaches the merge agent with a false report and no site, so its fix rests on the merge agent re-deriving what the verb should have found; evidence: the review backlog output quoted above; SKILL.md 'An issue whose problem names no file the run may edit adds no report: the verb lists it under settled, with files: []'.

The relevance pass runs once, at Resolve, against the draft as it stood then. After it, the work changes three ways and none of them goes back through it. (1) SKILL.md section 10: 'Where a planner's Docspecs: line names a docspec no work item names, add its Update the documentation per docspec:<slug> work item as a call'. This adds a new work item. (2) Section 10, kickback: 'it goes back to the draft, where you reshape it into the feature, script, or seed asset ... as a call'. This reshapes a work item. A call that answers an open issue meets none of the three. So a call, a new work item, or a reshaped one can answer an unruled issue that the relevance pass judged INDEPENDENT against the earlier draft, and the owner is never asked. The story promises: 'so that any executor can realize my intent without re-deriving it or deciding my open questions for me'. decision:relevance-scoped-queue-gate says: 'building over a bearing issue decides it silently' and 'When you cannot tell, it answers that the issue bears.' Where `.ok-planner/surface/surface.md` exists, check each piece of new user-facing surface the work introduces ... against the surface intent". Where the file does not exist the session skips the test entirely, and no step of the skill (nor artifact-definitions.md, core.md, sprint-document.md) tells the session to draft a `### New surface intent` delta or to ask the owner about each new element. Nothing else creates the file now that /audit is retired: a fresh true-up places none, and this repository itself has none. Evidence: stack up run-ca895d6c52e3 (git init scratch project), `bash plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up` from it exited 0 with "Trued up ok-planner at .../project (v26.0.0).", and `ls .ok-planner/surface` printed "ls: .ok-planner/surface: No such file or directory"; at the repo root `ls -la .ok-planner/surface/` printed the same; `grep -rn "New surface intent" plugins/` finds only the delta form in artifact-definitions.md:263, no instruction to draft one. So in every project without an intent, each new command, route, or env var a sprint adds ships without the owner deciding whether it is public. The story promises: "a way to decide whether each new user-facing element of my project is public before it ships, so that no element becomes part of my public surface unless I chose it." Decision surface-intent-changed-by-sprints: "Planning checks every new command, route, or other user-facing element the drafted work introduces against the intent. An element no rule of the intent claims is a question to the owner, and the answer becomes a surface-intent delta in the same sprint." With no intent, no rule claims any element, so every new element should be a question and the answer a `### New surface intent` delta.

It follows "An unclaimed one is one prose question to the owner", and overrides it: an element no rule of the intent claims, but that realizes a story, is taken as public by the session without a question, and the paragraph says no delta is drafted for it (the delta is drafted only "on the answer"), so the intent still claims nothing for the element after the sprint ships it. Decision surface-intent-changed-by-sprints, Choice: "An element no rule of the intent claims is a question to the owner, and the answer becomes a surface-intent delta in the same sprint." Step 13 says: 'For each vetoed row, file one issue with .ok-planner/bin/issues file --from - ... kind human, category product-intent, its problem the row and the owner's words, for the next /plan-sprint.' The owner's words go into problem, never into a ruling: 'issues list --json' after filing printed 'veto-calls-made-in-my-absence-cert-i1 open None True' (state open, ruling None, waiting True). An unruled issue goes to /triage-issues, whose triage prompt sorts 'a problem whose one option fixes a code site' as a defect claim and routes it 'retired' 'Where no entry covers a harm the code causes today'; a vetoed decline or rejection is exactly a harm a fixer or merge agent already judged the accept list leaves standing, so triage closes the owner's veto as retired. The story promises: 'a way to see every call made while I was away, so that I can overturn one I disagree with.' The completion-report concept: 'it puts every call before the owner at once, so the owner can veto any call they disagree with.' Saw: a veto filed per step 13 is an unruled product-intent issue that an agent may retire or answer, or carry with the agent's own recommended ruling, so the overturn does not stand on the owner's word.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md step 13. What the code does: 'For each vetoed row, file one issue with .ok-planner/bin/issues file --from - ... kind human, category product-intent, its problem the row and the owner's words, for the next /plan-sprint.' The owner's words land in problem and no ruling is written: in the driver's scratch project 'issues list --json' printed 'veto-calls-made-in-my-absence-cert-i1 open None True' (state open, ruling None, waiting True). Trigger: the owner vetoes a row at the close. Harm (C4): the unruled issue goes to /triage-issues, which may retire it as a defect claim no entry covers (a vetoed decline is one a fixer already judged the list leaves standing) or route it with its own recommended ruling that silence accepts, so the overturn does not stand on the owner's word. The artifact definitions have /plan-sprint transcribe 'a decision a person gives live, under that person's name' with 'issues rule'; story veto-calls-made-in-my-absence 'so that I can overturn one I disagree with'; concept completion-report 'so the owner can veto any call they disagree with'. The implementation notes' call for work item 9 asked for this filing. Scope: caused by the change (step 13's veto is new, B103). A change to step 13's text adds the removed lines to retired-boilerplate.json, as work item 9 did. From failure i51, driver t25.
note: Rewrote step 13 of How to execute this sprint in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md: each vetoed row's issue now carries the row as its problem, and the session then records the owner's words as its ruling with '.ok-planner/bin/issues rule <id> --text -', signed with the session person's name (relaying the setting text and ruling once a name resolves where it refuses, as /plan-sprint's Promote does). The issue is filed ruled, so /plan-sprint pulls it in as the owner's decision and /triage-issues cannot retire or re-recommend it. The removed lines were never in a released template: checks/sprint-boilerplate passes with retired-boilerplate.json unchanged. Files changed: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up, apply_plan with plumbline_estate_steps and lint_config_refusal. B32 drops .ok-plumbline/subjects/, practices/, subjects.md, practices.md (corpus) and .ok-plumbline/audits/, budget.json, .plumbline-budget.json (record) from scripts/review::OWNER_PATHS, ruled 'migrate: true-up removes or archives those estates in the plan that writes the new tool'. Where .ok-plumbline/ is blocked (unmerged paths or tracked files missing), plumbline_estate_steps adds blocked lines and returns before any move; where .ok-planner/config.json already exists, lint_config_refusal returns early ('if os.path.lexists(planner_config) or not held or not plumbline_plan()["blocked"]: return'), so no refusal; apply_plan then runs every action and materialize_steps writes the new .ok-planner/bin/review while the estate stays. Trigger: /ok on a project whose .ok-plumbline/ estate is blocked and whose .ok-planner/config.json exists. Harm (R2): the old user neither keeps the corpus and record classes nor gets a refusal; review owner prints project for the owner's .ok-plumbline/subjects/*.md, practices/*.md, and audit records, so review changed lists them and a /converge fixer may edit them. The notes-review call covers only the config-absent case. Evidence: true-up:3801-3807 (blocked return), true-up:4269-4271 (early return), true-up:4357-4371 (apply runs every action); scripts/review diff removing '.ok-plumbline/subjects/', '.ok-plumbline/audits/'. Scope: caused by the change. Reports: i49.
note: Added PLUMBLINE_CLASSED (.ok-plumbline/subjects, practices, audits, subjects.md, practices.md, budget.json, and root .plumbline-budget.json: the paths B32 drops from review::OWNER_PATHS) and plumbline_classes_refusal in admin/true-up, called from build_plan after lint_config_refusal: where plumbline_plan() is blocked and any of those paths holds a file on disk or in git, the plan carries a blocked line and a refusal, so every apply (bare or --go-ahead) refuses whole before any write, whether or not .ok-planner/config.json exists, and the new review tool is never written beside an unmigrated estate. Driven on a scratch project (config present, tracked file missing): diagnose prints the blocked line, true-up refuses 'nothing written'; once settled, no blocked line. ADMINISTRATION.md's go-ahead refusal list and the ok-plumbline migration paragraph name the new refusal. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md
