body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md, {{DOCUMENTATION-RULE}} and the C5 row of {{SPRINT-CATALOG}}; converge/prompts/sprint-pass.md, the documentation pass row. What the text does: the builder writes 'for the reader its ## Reader names, covering what its ## Covers names, and keeping its ## Notes. Decide which files under the Where to add, change, or drop.' (shared.md:111-114); C5 (shared.md:302) and the documentation pass (sprint-pass.md:28) report only 'each departure from the docspec's ## Reader, ## Covers, or ## Notes'. The docspec form says '## Where opens with the path: one file, or a folder, its path ending in /. For a folder, the lines after the path say how its files are laid out.' (_shared/artifact-definitions.md:169). Trigger: a docspec for a folder of documentation whose ## Where states a layout, such as 'docs/' then 'One file per command, named after the command.' Harm (A3): the builder is told to decide the files itself, and certification never checks the layout, so the owner's declared layout binds neither the writer nor the check. Story declare-project-documentation: 'so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; concept docspec: 'It says where that documentation lives'. In scope: the rule, C5, and the pass are new in this sprint (WI 4). Failure: i9.
note: Bound the docspec's Where layout. _sprint/shared.md {{DOCUMENTATION-RULE}}: the builder's 'Decide which files under the Where to add, change, or drop' now adds 'for a folder, lay them out as the lines after its path say'. {{SPRINT-CATALOG}} C5 adds 'the files under a folder's Where depart from the layout the lines after its path state'. converge/prompts/sprint-pass.md documentation row reports 'each file under a folder's ## Where that departs from the layout the lines after its path state'. The writer is now bound to the declared layout and certification checks it. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/sprint-pass.md

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/fix.md, the Fix steps; converge/prompts/verify.md, Read; {{PROSE-SCOPE-RULE}} in _converge/coding-rules.md. What the text does: the fixer is told 'Change nothing the defect does not need: no rename, no reshaping, no fix of something you happened to notice.' (fix.md:24) and nothing about documentation a docspec governs; the verifier checks 'the change, and only the change' (verify.md:9) against the accept list and boundaries, never a docspec; the review reads once before any fix, so nothing re-reads documentation after a fix. Trigger: a sprint-certification fix changes an observable behavior (a flag, a message, an output format) that the documentation under a docspec describes. Harm (A3): the fix lands in the sprint's commit while that documentation still describes the pre-fix behavior, and the next /plan-sprint's reconcile window starts after that commit, so nothing catches it. Story keep-documentation-current: 'each change to my product bring the documentation it affects along in the same change, so that the documentation a reader finds at any commit describes the product at that commit'. In scope: the promise that documentation moves with each sprint change is new in this sprint (WI 4, decision sprints-write-the-documentation), and the fix prompt's documentation lines changed in it. Failure: i17.
note: converge/prompts/fix.md Fix gains step 4: where the run certifies a sprint and the fix changes a behavior a user can observe, the fixer reads .ok-planner/docspec.md and, for each docspec a changed file falls under by a code-path reference, edits each sentence under its ## Where the fix made false, per the docspec, as part of the fix (old step 4 is now 5). converge/prompts/verify.md Read gains step 4 (the index, each such docspec, its documentation) and the fixed check adds 'no sentence in the documentation Read step 4 names states what the change made false'. _converge/coding-rules.md {{PROSE-SCOPE-RULE}} puts in review documentation under a docspec whose ## References the sprint's change, its certification fixes included, reaches, so the fixer may make that edit and the verifier does not send it back. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/fix.md, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/verify.md, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_converge/coding-rules.md

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md, Draft's 'The documentation match' paragraph, and core.md CODE-PLANNER-PROMPT step 8. What the text does: a docspec is touched only where 'its references include a corpus artifact a work item or delta names, or a code path the owner names for the work' (SKILL.md:105), read from the index .ok-planner/docspec.md; code planning matches only 'a path under Changes falls under one of its code-path references' (core.md:296). A '### New docspec' or '### Amend docspec' delta names the docspec itself, not one of its references, and a new docspec is not in the index until execution applies the delta. Trigger: an owner declares a new kind of documentation, or amends an existing docspec's ## Reader or ## Covers, through a docspec delta. Harm (A3, a skill surface that gives a wrong result): the sprint that carries the delta gets no 'Update the documentation per docspec:<slug>' work item, so no builder writes the documentation the new or amended order asks for (the build rule writes only where 'A builder whose work item names docspec:<slug>', _sprint/shared.md:109-110) and certification runs no documentation pass for it ('one pass per docspec a work item names', converge/prompts/sprint-review.md:26); the documentation keeps answering the old order until an unrelated change reaches a reference. Story declare-project-documentation: 'so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; decision sprints-write-the-documentation: 'adds one work item for each docspec the work touches'. In scope: the documentation match is new in this sprint (WI 3). Failures: i7 (variant kind, new docspec), i8 (variant reader, amended docspec).
note: Partial, staged: plan-sprint/SKILL.md Estate now skips the Draft docspec steps only past the draft's own New docspec deltas; The documentation match reads a New/Amend docspec delta's Where and References in place of its index row and counts every docspec such a delta carries as touched. core.md CODE-PLANNER-PROMPT inputs and step 8 take each docspec delta in place of its row. Left: scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md lines 172-174 still say 'Where docspec/ is missing ... planning skips the docspec steps', which the Estate change makes false for a sprint whose New docspec delta adds the first docspec.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/sprint-review.md, the documentation pass bullet; C5 in _sprint/shared.md {{SPRINT-CATALOG}}; {{PROSE-SCOPE-RULE}} in _converge/coding-rules.md. What the text does: certification cuts '`documentation`: one pass per docspec a work item names' and 'A sprint whose work items name no docspec has no documentation pass' (sprint-review.md:26); C5's 'the change reached the docspec's references and its documentation did not move' applies only to 'a docspec a work item names' (shared.md:302); a fixer may edit documentation only 'under the ## Where of a docspec ... that a work item of that sprint names' (coding-rules.md:54-55). Nothing checks whether the change reached the references of a docspec no work item names. Trigger: a builder whose stage widened its files past the notes' Changes (an 'outside files:' refile), or a certification fix, changes a code path a docspec's ## References names, and no work item names that docspec. Harm (A3): the sprint's commit carries code the docspec's documentation no longer describes, certification reports nothing, no fixer may move the documentation, and the next /plan-sprint's reconcile window ('<closed>..HEAD', with <closed> that sprint's own commit) starts after it, so no step ever flags it. Story keep-documentation-current: 'each change to my product bring the documentation it affects along in the same change, so that the documentation a reader finds at any commit describes the product at that commit'; decision sprints-write-the-documentation: 'Sprint certification reviews each touched documentation against its docspec and the change'. In scope: the documentation pass and C5 are new in this sprint (WI 4). Failure: i15.
note: Partial, staged: _sprint/shared.md {{SPRINT-REVIEW-READING}} gains step 6 (the docspec index; the change reaches a docspec where a file step 2 lists falls under a code-path reference, or a delta amends or retires an artifact it names; read each reached docspec no work item names). converge/prompts/sprint-review.md cuts a documentation pass per such docspec too, and the brief and close result name them. C5 covers a docspec whose references the change reached, the 'did not move' clause kept to a named docspec; sprint-pass.md's row matches. {{PROSE-SCOPE-RULE}} admits documentation under a docspec whose ## References the sprint's change, its certification fixes included, reaches. Left: converge/SKILL.md lines 15, 40, and 101 still describe the documentation passes and the prose scope as 'per docspec a work item names' only.

body: DOCSPEC-DEFINITION ## Lists bullet (and the listing rule in _sprint/shared.md DOCUMENTATION-RULE, sprint-pass.md documentation pass, C5): an element of a class the surface intent keeps internal that an exception makes public. Readings: (a) a reference docspec's ## Lists may name such a class, and the listing gives only its public exceptions; (b) ## Lists names only classes public by default, and public exceptions of internal classes reach a reference some other way (every reference lists them, or the owner adds a class). Built (a): the bullet now reads 'a class whose rule makes its members public, or one whose exceptions make a member public'. Decision surface-members-listed-at-need speaks of listing 'the members of each class'; the story reference-names-the-public-surface decides public-only.

The documentation match (SKILL.md Draft) and core.md CODE-PLANNER-PROMPT step 8: how a change to a listed class reaches a reference docspec. Readings: (a) derive the reach: a docspec with ## Lists is reached by a change under a file the surface intent names as declaring a class it lists, or by a surface intent delta that changes such a class's rule, exception, or declaring line; (b) require a reference docspec's ## References to name those declaring files (enforced by the compliance reviewer), leaving the match on references alone, which misses surface intent deltas and declaring files the intent adds later. Built (a), in SKILL.md, core.md inputs and step 8, the docspec definition's ## Lists bullet, and the certification reading's step 6 in _sprint/shared.md.

SKILL.md sections 6 and 12, core.md RELEVANCE-PASS-PROMPT: work and calls added after Resolve. Readings: (a) re-dispatch the relevance pass at Approval over the work items, deltas, and calls added or reshaped since Resolve, against the unruled issues the walk did not take up, and walk what bears; (b) hand the code planner the unruled open issues and have it raise a question wherever a call would answer one, which leaves the session's own calls (section 10's documentation work item, kickback reshapes) unchecked. Built (a), with a Scope input and a call bullet in the relevance prompt's test.

Two readings: the story true-up-project-estate says 'so that upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote', under which the rewrite should archive a copy first or count as destructive; the decision whole-file-ownership's Choice says 'True-up rewrites a suite-owned file that carries its stamp or its fixed content with no question', and its 'so true-up never discards uncommitted work' sentence governs removals only, under which the loss is accepted since the stamped file is suite-owned and tells the owner project rules belong in their own files. body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md) and the sprint template's completion contract (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md). SKILL.md sprint step 4 says: 'Where review stories prints no slug, or review drive-stack prints unfilled or refuses, skip the drive, and say so in the return with the reason.' Drive step 2, which sprint step 4 runs, says: 'Where the start fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, ... and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds.' The return block is still presented, and the contract (sprint-document.md lines 274-279) requires only that the report 'carries the return block ... the run's find loop ran once, and every defect stands verified, declined, duplicate, or stuck'. So a sprint whose certification drove no story (a transient stack-start failure, or the seeded project.md, whose Drive commands section a fresh true-up leaves unfilled: 'review drive-stack' printed 'unfilled' in a scratch project trued up from the working tree) meets the same contract as a sprint whose every story was driven. By contrast, a review root that fails twice presents no return block, 'so the completion report carries no certification and the completion contract stays open' (SKILL.md line 101): the review not running holds done open, the drive not running does not. The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'; decision drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user's Choice: 'sprint certification each give every story its own driver once per run'; and sprint-document.md step 12 tells the executor certification judges that 'a user gets what every story promises when a driver uses the running product'. Saw: two sprints of one project can both close done, one with every story driven and one with none, and the contract text gives a checker no term that tells them apart. Evidence: scratch run run-3d4a975c8091: 'python3 .ok-planner/bin/review drive-stack' -> 'unfilled' (exit 0) after true-up.
note: certification-closes-done-with-no-story-driven

body: Reviewed /converge's Loop 2 against the story. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 says: 'A fix task that closed partial with a result starting outside files: waits for the task that held them: its fixer already widened those defects' files, so set its unfinished defects (those still fixing) back to open with kickbacks raised by one'. No fix of those defects was tried or sent back; they only waited on a file another task held. With the seeded fix.max_kickbacks of 2 (review/seed/config.json), a defect deferred once for file contention reaches stuck after a single verifier send-back, has its change backed out, and goes to the owner as a judgment issue. The skill's own premise says otherwise: 'A stuck defect's fix failed twice, so what fixes it is a judgment'. The story promises: 'defects across my product found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'; saw: the text routes to the owner a defect only one fix attempt failed, a question that needs no judgment by the skill's own rule; evidence: SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 (quoted above), Loop 2 step 1 ('Every defect at state open whose kickbacks field has reached config.json fix.max_kickbacks is set to stuck'), seed config 'fix': {'group_size': 4, 'max_kickbacks': 2}.

body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree, committed bin/clean (an extensionless shell script), filed a category: defect issue whose problem reads 'bin/clean:main runs rm -rf "$1"/ with no check; ... Accept entry A2.', and ran .ok-planner/bin/review backlog as /converge's backlog step says. It printed {"reports": [], "settled": [{"issue": "clean-empty-arg", "files": [], "left_alone": {}}]} (exit 0): the issue names an existing project file, yet the verb says it names none. scripts/review backlog_entry reads paths with PATH_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[\w./-]+\.\w+") and SITE_PATTERN, both of which need a file extension, so no extensionless file (bin/clean, scripts/review, scripts/tasks, admin/true-up, checks/run here) is ever taken as a file. SKILL.md then has the session add a report saying 'issue <id>: its problem names no file of this tree outside the exclude list', which is false, and the ownership routing for left_alone files never runs for extensionless suite files such as .ok-planner/bin/review. The story promises: defects across the product found and fixed without the owner; saw: a defect issue on an extensionless script reaches the merge agent with a false report and no site, so its fix rests on the merge agent re-deriving what the verb should have found; evidence: the review backlog output quoted above; SKILL.md 'An issue whose problem names no file the run may edit adds no report: the verb lists it under settled, with files: []'.
note: review-backlog-misses-extensionless-files

The skill never tells the session to relay that note: SKILL.md step 1 says only 'Say the run's shape in one line before it starts ... the count of changed files ...' and defines the changed files as 'every file added, changed, or deleted since the base under the project root and its declared folders', and analysis step 1 relays only the surface-intent note ('the verb says so on stderr and the run hunts file areas alone; say so in the return'). No line of the return block names it either. A session following the text runs analysis or sprint certification over the root alone and reports its hunt and its checks as passing, with nothing telling the owner that the code under the declared folders was skipped. body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-version/SKILL.md, the session-start hook it reads (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/hooks/session-start), and plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md; the story promises: 'a way to see which plugin version governs my current session beside the version this project's vendored layer carries, so that version drift is visible'; saw: the skill's 'Plugin version (governing this session)' is never a plugin's version. Step 1 reads it from the line 'ok-planner vX.Y.Z is materialized in this project', which the vendored hook emits from its own true-up stamp ('context="ok-planner v{{OK_PLANNER_VERSION}} is materialized in this project..."' in scripts/hooks/session-start), or from the 'Materialized by ok-planner v<X.Y.Z>' line of a vendored rules file. The skill itself says so: 'Both sources are written by the vendored layer the session started with, so the value equals the vendored stamp (step 2) unless an /ok run trued up the project during this session.' So both reported numbers are vendored-layer stamps, and the skill never reads the installed ok plugin's version (the front door that carries the ok-planner family; plugins/ok/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, readable through 'claude plugin list --json', which /ok step 1 already uses). The common drift is invisible: the user-scoped ok plugin is updated to a newer version (by /ok in another project, since plugin content is per machine) while this project stays vendored at the old one; /ok-version then prints the same version on both lines. The suite elsewhere names exactly that gap as the drift signal: /ok's report says '**carried** is the suite version the resolved payload carries ... **vendored in project** is the version the vendored layer's stamps record here ... The gap between the two columns is the useful signal'. The skill's description also names an 'ok-planner plugin version', but ok-planner is a family the ok plugin carries, not a plugin. evidence: SKILL.md step 1 and step 4 lines '- **Plugin version (governing this session):** <X.Y.Z or unknown>' and '- **Vendored layer (this project's stamp):** <X.Y.Z or —>', both sourced from vendored stamps.
note: ok-version-reports-no-plugin-version

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/sketch/SKILL.md against the story, then trued up a scratch project (run-8301c158cf44), wrote a sketch at the skill's path, and re-ran true-up: the skill lands at .claude/skills/sketch/, true-up creates .ok-planner/sketches/, and a second true-up leaves the sketch untouched. One divergence: the skill fixes the save path to the date and topic alone and never says what to do when that file exists. Step 4 reads: 'Write the sketch to .ok-planner/sketches/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-sketch.md using the template below, with today's date'. A second /sketch on the same topic the same day (a revision, or a rival take on the idea) therefore overwrites the first, which is never committed by the skill, so the earlier thinking is lost; the skill names no check for an existing file, no suffix, and no refusal. The story promises: 'so that thinking is externalized and revisitable at no ceremony cost'; the sketch concept says sketches give ideas 'a cheap, durable landing place so they are neither lost nor prematurely promoted'. saw: no text in the skill protects an existing sketch at the computed path; evidence: step 4 and the 'Save sketches to' line are the only path rules in the file.

body: In a scratch project (true-up of the working tree, dashboard page built from the tree's source), I seeded an upstream issue rule-on-the-whole-intake-q9 routed as triage-issues/SKILL.md's upstream row says (route upstream, three options: a workaround, a filing upstream, or both, and a recommended ruling 'File the draft with the ok suite.'), then on the dashboard page opened 'needs ruling', pressed j and then a (Accept the recommendation). The page recorded the ruling 'File the draft with the ok suite.' signed 'ruled by Rule Owner A'; issues show prints 'Ruling (2026-10-17T09:21:19Z): File the draft with the ok suite.'. I then read how the next /plan-sprint treats that ruled issue. plan-sprint/SKILL.md, Frame, 'Set the upstream issues apart': 'A ruling that names where the owner filed it, and asks for no workaround, is a filing upstream: record it now ... A ruling that names a workaround rides the sweep like any ruled issue ... A ruling that names neither cannot be understood: ask the owner about it, as above.' An accepted filing recommendation names an intent to file, not where it was filed, and no workaround, so Frame asks the owner about it again. The story promises: 'As a project owner, I want a way to rule on every open judgment issue in one sitting, so that my next planning session starts with no question left unanswered.' Saw: a ruling the product itself offers as one key (accept triage's recommended filing) on every upstream issue triage recommends filing reaches the next planning session as a question, so the session does not start with every question answered. The ruling the page offers and the ruling Frame can act on disagree: either Frame takes an accepted 'file upstream' ruling as the owner's answer (walking only the act of filing, or closing once a filing is named), or the page and the upstream recommendation tell the owner the ruling must name where it was filed. A ruling typed by hand that names a workaround ('file it upstream and pin the library meanwhile', issue rule-on-the-whole-intake-up) does ride the sweep. Evidence: page text after a: 'RULING / File the draft with the ok suite. / ruled by Rule Owner A2026-10-17T09:21:19Z · Withdraw ruling / UPSTREAM ISSUE / The suite hook times out after 5 s.'
note: accepted-upstream-recommendation-asked-again

The story promises: upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote; whole-file-ownership says 'so true-up never discards uncommitted work', and the removal rule archives a suite file with an uncommitted change rather than removing it. Saw: diagnose listed the overwrite as a non-destructive step, so the plan carried no question, and the true-up overwrote the file. The uncommitted lines are in no file of the tree, the archive, or HEAD, and no report line names them. Evidence: diagnose printed 'DRIFT: stale: .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md differs from the carried v26.0.0 rendering' and 'PLAN: 1 step(s), 0 destructive; plan 8c2a3d05b87e'; the bare true-up exited 0 with 'materialized: 1 files under .ok-planner/ and .claude/ (v26.0.0)' and 'Trued up ok-planner at .../c (v26.0.0).'; afterwards grep -rl C-UNCOMMITTED-OWNER-RULE over the tree found nothing, git grep over HEAD found nothing, and git status was clean. In the upgraded v26 project, a scan of every owner marker found every one kept but 'B-UNCOMMITTED-RULES-EDIT (HEAD: )', which was gone. body: Reviewed plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md, admin/ADMINISTRATION.md, and the admin/true-up core it drives, and ran the core against scratch projects. SKILL.md step 4.4 says 'A plan with no destructive step needs no question', and its Boundaries say 'Writes nothing the owner has not let proceed'. ADMINISTRATION.md defines DRIFT as 'a step that destroys nothing: writing or regenerating a suite file', and the core classes a rewrite of a stamped suite file as DRIFT whatever its git state. So a session that follows /ok overwrites an uncommitted owner edit in a stamped suite file (such as .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md) with no question, no archive, and no report line. The story promises: upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote; whole-file-ownership says 'so true-up never discards uncommitted work', and the removal rule ('Every other file the plan would remove — one with an uncommitted or staged-only change ... — moves to the archive instead') protects the same file when it is removed but not when it is rewritten. Evidence: in an upgrade from a v26.0.0 layout, diagnose printed 'DRIFT: stale: .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md differs from the carried v26.0.0 rendering' while the file carried the uncommitted line 'B-UNCOMMITTED-RULES-EDIT'; after the go-ahead the line was in no tree file and not in HEAD. In a current project, 'PLAN: 1 step(s), 0 destructive' was followed by a bare true-up (exit 0) that discarded 4 uncommitted lines; the core's own flow, which /ok follows, asked nothing. See the matching failure on the true-up core's command line.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md:The documentation match, and core.md {{CODE-PLANNER-PROMPT}} step 8. What the code does: a docspec is touched only where a work item or delta names a corpus artifact in its ## References, or a change path falls under one of its code-path references. SKILL.md:105: 'a docspec whose references include a corpus artifact a work item or delta names, or a code path the owner names for the work, is touched'; core.md:296: 'a docspec is reached where a path under Changes falls under one of its code-path references'. Neither the ## Lists classes, their declaring files under the surface intent's '## Where each class is declared', nor a surface intent delta reaches a reference docspec, and neither the docspec definition nor the compliance reviewer's Docspec form requires a reference docspec's References to cover them. Trigger: a sprint that adds a member to a listed class in a declaring file its References omit, or a surface intent delta that moves an element between public and internal. Harm (A8, story reference-names-the-public-surface 'name every element I made public and no element I kept internal'): no 'Update the documentation per docspec:<slug>' work item is added, so certification runs no documentation pass (sprint-review.md:26 'A sprint whose work items name no docspec has no documentation pass') and the reference goes stale with nothing noticing. Evidence: driver ran catalog-toc on a scratch reference docspec whose ## Lists names 'CLI verbs'; the index row shows only where and references. Scope: caused by the change (the documentation match is new). From failure i22, driver t15.
note: confirm drive: reviewed plan-sprint/SKILL.md The documentation match, core.md CODE-PLANNER-PROMPT inputs and step 8, _sprint/shared.md SPRINT-REVIEW-READING step 6, artifact-definitions.md DOCSPEC-DEFINITION Lists; ran catalog-toc on a scratch project whose one docspec cli-reference has '## References - `src/other.py`' and '## Lists - CLI verbs'. The new text reaches a Lists docspec through declaring files and the surface intent delta in all three places, but each place keys the reach on 'A docspec with a ## Lists section' while telling the reader to match against the docspec index, and the index still does not say which docspecs have ## Lists, the gap the earlier driver's evidence named. SKILL.md: 'read the docspec index at .ok-planner/docspec.md ... Match the drafted work against every row ... A docspec with a ## Lists section is touched too where ...: read each such docspec's ## Lists from the docspec'; core.md inputs: 'The docspec index ... For each docspec with a ## Lists section, read its ## Lists'; shared.md step 6: 'The docspec index .ok-planner/docspec.md ... For a docspec with a ## Lists section'.
